CheckReport.description:
What `check` prints: the counts, the links to show, and the findings not tied to one link

JSON puts `summary` and `links` under `data`; the envelope carries the loose findings. Passed
links are always counted but listed only under `--verbose`.

code_blocks.description:
The code blocks shown: the ones not passed, or every one under `--verbose`. Absent
when `[features.code-blocks]` is off.

links.description: The links shown, each with the finding that explains its state.

summary.description: How many links are in each state, passed ones included, and how many code blocks.

CheckSummary.description:
`data.summary`: the link counts flattened, with the code block counts beside them when
`[features.code-blocks]` is on.

broken.description: Links whose target can't be found.

code_blocks.description: How many code blocks are in each state.

failed.description: Links whose target changed since the doc was confirmed.

new.description: Links with no lock entry yet.

obsolete.description: Lock entries whose link no longer exists.

passed.description: Links whose target still matches the lockfile.

CodeBlockCounts.description:
How many blocks are in each state, and how many steps were off, skipped or due but not run.
`blocks` is the sum of the state counts; the step counts are apart from them, so a block whose
format step is off and whose lint step passed counts in both `passed` and `format_off`.

failed.description: Blocks with a failed check or a missing excerpt source.

format_not_run.description:
Format steps due on a checked block that didn't run, such as a formatter supdoc couldn't
run safely.

format_off.description: Format steps off: blocks whose formatter's table sets `format = "off"`.

format_skipped.description: Format steps skipped: blocks the author marked `format(off: ...)`.

lint_not_run.description: Lint steps due on a checked block that didn't run, such as clippy, which needs trust.

lint_off.description: Lint steps off: blocks whose linter's table sets `lint = "off"`.

lint_skipped.description: Lint steps skipped: blocks the author marked `lint(off: ...)`.

not_checked.description: Blocks nothing checked: text, a language turned off, or no step that ran.

stale.description: Excerpts that differ from their source.

tool_missing.description: Blocks whose selected tool isn't installed.

unknown_language.description: Blocks in a language supdoc has no checker for.

CodeBlockJson.description: One code block as `check --json` shows it.

file.description: The doc or source file, relative to the project root.

format.description: What the format step did: `ran`, `off`, `skipped` or `not_run`.

language.description: The language tag the block is read as. Left out for an untagged block outside Rust docs.

lint.description: What the lint step did: `ran`, `off`, `skipped` or `not_run`.

reason.description: Why the block is in that state, when it has a reason.

state.description:
`passed`, `failed`, `stale`, `opted_out`, `not_checked`, `unknown_language` or
`tool_missing`: `failed` when a step that ran failed, `passed` when the steps that ran all
passed.

uses.description: Each `uses(...)` target the block writes, with its state.

FindingJson.description: A finding as JSON shows it.

fix.description: The one correct edit, when there is exactly one.

location.description: Where it is. Left out of a link's nested finding, which shares the link's location.

FixJson.description: An exact edit as JSON shows it, with byte offsets so a script can apply it without recounting.

file.description: The file to edit, relative to the project root.

LinkJson.description:
One link as `check --json` and `list --json` show it.

`source`, `target` and `symbol` sit beside the state. The explaining finding is nested
without a location, since `locations` already says where the link is.

finding.description: The finding that explains the state. Left out for `passed`.

locations.description: Every place it appears in its source. Empty only for `obsolete`.

source.description: The file the link is written in.

symbol.description:
`None` = whole file. `Option`'s ordering puts whole-file entries first. Left out of JSON
when `None`.

target.description: The file the link points at.

LinkLocationJson.description: Where a link appears in its source. The file is the link's `source`, so it isn't repeated.

LinkState.description:
Where one link stands, in snapshot-testing terms.

The same values name states everywhere: in reports, in `--state` filters on `update` and
`list`, and in JSON output.

oneOf.description: The target's hash matches the lock entry.
The target's hash differs from the lock entry: the code changed since the doc was confirmed.
The target file, symbol or namespace can't be found.
The link has no lock entry yet.
A lock entry whose link no longer exists.

LocationJson.description: A place in a file as JSON shows it.

file.description: The file, relative to the project root.

SeverityJson.description: A severity as JSON shows it.

SourcePath.description: A file path relative to the project root, with `/` separators.

SymbolPath.description: A dotted symbol path such as `Config.validate`.

UseJson.description: One `uses(...)` target of a code block and where it stands against the lockfile.

UseState.description: Where one `uses(...)` target stands against the lockfile.

oneOf.description: The symbol's hash is the recorded one.
The symbol changed since it was recorded.
The lockfile doesn't record it for this doc.

description:
The one object every command writes under `--json`, with the same top-level keys each time.

Its schema is the one `supdoc schema` prints, so the JSON written and the schema published
come from this one type.

findings.description: Findings that aren't about one link.

ok.description: `true` exactly when the exit code is 0.

root.description: The absolute project root, which every other path is relative to.

title: Envelope
